headline: Approved June 29 minutes as amended; discussed status of Huntress, Hovey, Clough, Powers, Fernald, and other trust funds.
summary: The Commission approved the June 29 meeting minutes as amended. It reviewed fund balances and discussed the status of several trust funds, including the Huntress, Hovey, Ornamental Tree, Clough Vocational School, Margaret Irving Powers Memorial, Fernald, and Babson House funds. No disbursements were finalized; several follow-up actions were assigned, and the next meeting was set for October 6th at 9:30am.
decisions: Approved the June 29, 2026 meeting minutes as amended.

decision_evidence.quote: A MOTION was made to approve the minutes of the June 29th meeting. There were no changes. The motion was seconded. All were in favor. The minutes were approved, as amended.

plain_text:
Board of Commissioners of Trust Funds Meeting Minutes 
City of Gloucester 
City Hall- First Floor Conference Room 
9 Dale Ave 
Gloucester, Ma 01930 
Monday, August 12, 2026 
 
Present: Karen N. Bell (Chair), Frederica Doeringer (co-Chair), John Bourneuf (Clerk), Linda Pata 
(CASB) and Rocco DeFilippis (Asst General Counsel). 
This meeting was organized around the following agenda: 
1. Opening remarks from Commissioner Karen Bell 
2. Vote for approval of minutes from meeting of June 29, 2026 
3. Review of current balances from Funds and explanation of Huntress Fund size and 
location:   Linda Pata.  
4. Status of 5 funds with disbursements authorized in January 2026 or earlier and the 
ornamental tree fund transferred to DPW. 
5. Update on status of Powers and Clough Funds with reference to probate court decrees 
• Margaret Irving Powers Memorial Fund 
• Clough Vocational School Fund 
6. Report from Rocco DeFilippis about his research on Action and the Housing Authority 
related to the Fernald Fund with MA AG Office 
7. Ideas for disbursements from accumulated income of Huntress Funds:  Discussion all 
8. Overall strategy for the remaining funds: Discussion All 
9. Dates for future meetings 
 
1 & 2.  The meeting was called to order at approximately 9:35am.  To start off the meeting there 
were a few opening remarks from Commissioner Karen Bell and a review of the agenda for the 
meeting.  It was noted that we were not able to broadcast live due to connectivity issues.  After 
discussion of changes needed, A MOTION was made to approve the minutes of the June 29th 
meeting.  There were no changes. The motion was seconded.  All were in favor.  The minutes 
were approved, as amended.  ACTION #1: Jock will delete the Draft watermark and send the 
June minutes to Lee O’Leary to post the minutes on the City of Gloucester site. 
 
3. There was not much discussion regarding funds balances.  The Commissioners all had a copy 
of the April 1 – June 30th fund balances. 
 
4. The Commission next discussed whether there had been distribution of the five funds 
(Sawyer Medal & Ornamental Tree Fund, Sawyer Drawing & Music Fund, Books & Stationery for
Poor Children, Benjamin M. Smith Fund and the Great Republic Fund).  In Conor MacCorkle’s 
absence, there was no status.  Karen said that she had sent Conor an e-mail on August 6th and 
there was no response yet.  It was noted that the city just went through the budgeting process; 
that could be why there has been no response.  It was also noted that Conor might be on 
vacation.  ACTION #1 – Karen will follow-up with Conor. 
 
While on the topic of approved disbursements, the Commissioners discussed the Hovey Fund.  
A $10,000 disbursement was authorized in December, and it was not known if a check was ever 
sent to the intended recipient.  ACTION #2 - Karen to also ask Conor if this transaction had been 
processed.  The process is such that the city first sends a check to the recipient and then 
requests CASB to send the city a check of the same magnitude.  Linda said she has not seen a 
payment from CASB.  But, once this transaction is confirmed to be completed, the fund balance 
will drop below the $75,000 “administrative” hurdle and can be grouped with the others 
approved by the AG’s office. 
 
Karen also noted that the action to disburse funds from the Ornamental Tree Fund was also 
with Conor MacCorkle.  She is also waiting to hear back and will mention to Conor in the above 
correspondence (ACTION #3).  
 
5. Rocco next provided an update on the Clough Vocational School Fund and the Margaret Irving 
Powers Memorial Fund.  Amy Pasquarello, the new Superintendent of Gloucester Public 
Schools, is reviewing the proposal for only the Clough Fund to coordinate with the Gloucester 
School Committee.  Regarding the Margaret Irving Powers Memorial Fund, it was noted that 
Gloucester DPW is the Administrator of the monies from this Fund. 
 
6. Rocco briefly discussed the Fernald Fund status.  The original thinking was that the Health 
Department or the Youth Prevention Team were potential recipients.  If it was to go to the Youth 
Prevention Team, perhaps this distribution could be combined with the Tufts Charity Fund.   
 
ACTION #4 – Rocco will continue to work with the AG’s office for the Clough and Fernald Funds 
and work iterations of the petition drafts with the AG’s office. 
 
7. The Huntress Fund was discussed next.  Karen & Freddie discussed the results of their 
inquiries with the Gloucester Housing Authority, The Rose Baker Center and Action Inc.  On 
August 6th, Karen Bell provided the following summary e-mail of her conversation with Gail 
Campbell at the Gloucester Housing Authority.  She noted that many of the past funds have 
come from the State for Section 8 housing.  The e-mail goes on… 
 
“Gail spent 11 years working as a social worker for the Gloucester Housing Authority.  The 
Housing Authority is a state/city agency that issues housing vouchers for qualifying individuals.
Gail said that many elderly people are very low-income and have difficulty finding housing.  She 
said that Action Inc. frequently helps people move into subsidized housing but that often people 
don't have the money to pay for a mover, buy new/used furniture, transport it, and pay deposits 
and other fees for housing.  She thought that Action would be a good recipient of monies 
intended to keep elderly people from becoming homeless or put in uncomfortable situations 
with relatives.”  It appears that the Huntress Home did essentially this for poor elderly women.  
Senior Care just provides personal home care services for elderly, many with medical needs.”  It 
was further noted that funding from the Huntress Fund will just be the current accumulated 
income from the fund, not the principal. 
ACTION #5 – Freddie to draft an RFP.  This may be based on an old draft already completed 
 
8. The Babson House was also discussed briefly at the end of the meeting.  Rocco noted that the 
petition for this fund is being worked with the AG’s office.  It was noted that this fund does not 
fall under the purview and responsibility of the Commission.   
 
A motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting at 10:40am.  All approved.  The 
Commission agreed to meet again on October 6th at 9:30am in the 1st floor conference room, 
Gloucester City Hall. 
 
Respectfully submitted 
 
 
John Bourneuf, Clerk
